slides.title: The OrchestrAI Bible
slides.subtitle: Module 3 · Governance-First Setup
slides.opening_hook: Modules 1 and 2 established the mindset. Module 3 establishes the discipline that makes the mindset operational.
bullets: Five acts. Twenty-three slides. The complete pre-engagement playbook for a real client project.
We will establish OGE — Observability, Guardrails, Evaluation — as the framework's spine.
Two reusable master prompts will be provided as artifacts to retain.
The OrchestrAI Issue Tracker engagement runs as our case study throughout.
slides.closing_thread: We begin with the foundational mandate that governs every engagement.
slides.narration: Module three. The bible. Five acts, twenty-three slides, the complete pre-engagement playbook. We establish OGE, deliver two reusable master prompts, and walk the OrchestrAI Issue Tracker engagement as our case study throughout.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Welcome to Module 3 of the OrchestrAI Lead Certification.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Modules 1 and 2 established the mindset and lifecycle. Module 3 establishes the discipline that makes the mindset operational.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Five acts. We will introduce the OGE framework — Observability, Guardrails, and Evaluation — as the spine of every OrchestrAI engagement. We will provide two reusable master prompts as artifacts to retain.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: And throughout, we anchor each principle to the OrchestrAI Issue Tracker — a production engagement that we will refer to repeatedly. Let us begin.

slides.title: Quality is not a service. It is a mandate.
slides.subtitle: The foundational principle of OrchestrAI delivery

hero_stat.label: of OrchestrAI engagements operate under OGE — without exception

analogy.title: Safety in a high-performance vehicle
analogy.text: A high-performance vehicle without safety systems is not premium engineering — it is a liability. OrchestrAI delivers production-ready outcomes in seven days because OGE is engineered in from the first prompt, never appended as an afterthought.

bullets: Clients do not contract for security as a line item. They assume it is the baseline.
Acceleration without governance produces production incidents that erode client trust.
OGE is the mechanism that allows the same engagement to claim both 'delivered in seven days' and 'passed security review on day eight'.
Every certified Lead internalises the mandate: Quality is not a service. It is a mandate.
slides.closing_thread: With the mandate established, we examine the two engagement entry points.
slides.narration: Quality is not a service. It is a mandate. This principle governs every OrchestrAI engagement. Clients do not contract for security as a line item — they assume it as baseline. OGE is the mechanism that lets the same engagement claim both rapid delivery and security review pass.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: If you retain one sentence from this module, retain this one.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Quality is not a service. It is a mandate.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Clients do not contract for security as a line item. They assume it as the baseline. The day your AI-built application leaks data is the day your acceleration advantage evaporates.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: OGE is precisely the mechanism that permits us to claim both rapid delivery and security review pass — simultaneously, in the same engagement.

slides.subtitle: Approach A · client-led    versus    Approach B · builder-led

slides.narration: Two engagement entry points. Approach A is client-led — they provide the stack, the UI, the standards. Approach B is builder-led — they provide only the intent, and the Lead conducts analysis. Both converge on identical governance setup.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: An important point that practitioners often overlook.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Not every client arrives with crystallised requirements. Some hand you a forty-page specification. Others say, in effect, 'build us something useful'.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Two approaches address this. Approach A — client-led discovery. Approach B — builder-led analysis. Both converge on the same governance setup.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Different entry ramps. Identical destination. The discipline does not change with the entry point.

slides.subtitle: When the client conveys the problem, not the plan

analogy.text: The client describes the outcome and trusts the Lead to determine the means. The Lead performs structured analysis, proposes options, secures client selection — converting the engagement to Approach A from that point forward.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram

slides.title: OGE — Observability · Guardrails · Evaluation
slides.subtitle: Enterprise-grade assurance at delivery speed

analogy.title: The three-legged construct
analogy.text: Remove any one leg and the construct collapses. Observability without Guardrails produces transparent disorder. Guardrails without Evaluation produces enforced rules without verification. Evaluation without Observability produces blind testing. All three are required.

list.name: Observability
list.desc: Traceability and transparency by design. Every AI prompt, every code commit, every business event is logged. No opaque behaviour.

list.name: Guardrails
list.desc: Policies, templates, and technical controls that bound AI action — from prompt structure through CI/CD deployment gates.

list.name: Evaluation
list.desc: Continuous multi-layer quality and risk verification — functional, security, performance, AI output, regression. Not a late phase.

slides.memory_hook: Observability — see what occurred. Guardrails — define what is permitted. Evaluation — verify that quality has held.
slides.closing_thread: We examine each pillar in turn, beginning with Observability.
slides.narration: OGE — three pillars. A three-legged construct. Observability is to see what occurred. Guardrails is to define what is permitted. Evaluation is to verify that quality has held. All three are required.

slides.title: Observability — Full Transparency by Design
slides.subtitle: Pillar 1 of 3

analogy.title: Flight recorder principle
analogy.text: Commercial aircraft do not operate without flight recorders. Every input, every output, every decision is logged so that — when something goes wrong, and eventually something will — engineers do not guess. They replay.

list.name: AI Interaction Logging
list.desc: All prompts and AI-generated responses are logged. Complete audit trail of how code and logic were produced.

list.name: Code Versioning
list.desc: AI-generated code committed to version control — Git. Full history, rollback capability, ownership clarity.

list.name: System Monitoring
list.desc: API logs, error tracking, performance metrics. Real-time visibility into system health.

list.name: Business Event Tracking
list.desc: Workflow-level logging — approvals, validations, state transitions. Transparent enforcement of business rules.

slides.memory_hook: No opaque behaviour. Every decision and output is explainable.
slides.reflection_prompt: Consider a system you operate today. If a defect arose, could a reviewer determine exactly what occurred and why? If not, that is an observability gap that OrchestrAI eliminates by design.
slides.closing_thread: Guardrails govern what AI is permitted to do.
slides.narration: Observability — four capabilities. AI interaction logging stores every prompt and response. Code versioning commits every AI-generated change to Git. System monitoring provides real-time visibility. Business event tracking logs workflow-level events. The outcome is that no system behaviour is opaque.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Observability is the flight recorder principle. Commercial aircraft do not operate without flight recorders.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Four capabilities. One — AI interaction logging. Every prompt and response is stored. The audit trail of how code came to exist.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Two — code versioning. Every AI-generated change committed to Git. Full history, rollback capability, ownership clarity.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Three — system monitoring. API logs, error tracking, performance metrics in real time.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Four — business event tracking. State transitions, approvals, validations all logged. Workflow behaviour becomes inspectable on demand.

slides.title: Guardrails — Enterprise Control Mechanisms
slides.subtitle: Pillar 2 of 3

analogy.title: Highway safety infrastructure
analogy.text: Highways install barriers not because drivers are incompetent, but because at high velocity there is no margin for error. The same principle applies to AI-accelerated development — at delivery speed, recovery from a security breach is not feasible.

list.name: Prompt Guardrails
list.desc: Structured requirement templates. Mandatory business rules and edge cases. Reduces ambiguous or unsafe AI outputs.

list.name: Code Guardrails
list.desc: Secure coding aligned to OWASP. Mandatory input validation and error handling. No deployment of unreviewed AI-generated code.

list.name: Access Control
list.desc: Role-based access control. Principle of least privilege. Server-side enforcement of authorisation on every request.

list.name: Data Protection
list.desc: No sensitive data in prompts. Masking or tokenisation where required. Alignment with GDPR, SOC 2, ISO 27001.

list.name: Deployment Guardrails
list.desc: Mandatory approval checkpoints. Security validation and test-pass criteria. Controlled CI/CD pipelines.

slides.memory_hook: Five categories — Prompt, Code, Access, Data, Deployment. Omitting any one constitutes a material risk.
slides.closing_thread: Evaluation completes the framework by verifying that the controls hold.
slides.narration: Guardrails — five categories. Prompt guardrails enforce structured templates. Code guardrails align to OWASP with no unreviewed deployment. Access control implements RBAC with server-side enforcement. Data protection prohibits sensitive data in prompts. Deployment guardrails establish controlled CI/CD with mandatory approval checkpoints.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Guardrails — the highway safety infrastructure of an AI-accelerated build. At delivery speed, recovery from a breach is not feasible.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Five categories. First, prompt guardrails. Structured templates with mandatory business rules and edge cases. This reduces ambiguous or unsafe AI outputs at source.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Second, code guardrails. OWASP-aligned secure coding. Mandatory input validation. Mandatory error handling. No deployment of unreviewed AI-generated code under any circumstances.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Third, access control. Role-based access control. Principle of least privilege. Server-side enforcement on every request — never client-side alone.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Fourth, data protection. Sensitive data is never inserted into prompts. Masking or tokenisation is required where data must be referenced. GDPR, SOC 2, and ISO 27001 alignment is non-negotiable.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Fifth, deployment guardrails. Controlled CI/CD pipelines. Approval checkpoints. Security validation prior to promotion. The pipeline itself functions as a guardrail.

slides.title: Evaluation — Continuous Quality Assurance
slides.subtitle: Pillar 3 of 3

analogy.title: Continuous quality versus end-of-line inspection
analogy.text: End-of-line inspection identifies defects after the product is complete. Continuous quality assurance prevents defects from being introduced at any stage. OrchestrAI implements the latter by design.

list.name: Functional
list.desc: Business requirement accuracy. Test cases mapped one-to-one to each requirement.

list.name: Security
list.desc: Static analysis security testing. Dependency vulnerability scans. Authentication and authorisation verification per route.

list.name: Performance
list.desc: Load testing. Response time benchmarks. Scalability validation.

list.name: AI Output
list.desc: Accuracy verification of generated logic. Edge-case validation. Hallucination checks.

list.name: Regression
list.desc: Automated regression suites executed on every meaningful update. Stability across changes.

slides.memory_hook: Five layers — Functional, Security, Performance, AI Output, Regression. Continuous, never deferred.
slides.closing_thread: We have established the framework. The ten mandatory practices that operationalise it follow.
slides.narration: Evaluation — five layers. Functional verifies business requirement accuracy. Security executes SAST scans and dependency vulnerability checks. Performance conducts load testing and benchmarking. AI output validates generated logic and checks for hallucinations. Regression runs automated suites on every meaningful update.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Evaluation is the third pillar. It is not a phase. It is not deferred to the end of the engagement. It is continuous.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Five layers. Functional — every business requirement has a corresponding test case. One-to-one mapping. No requirement is untested.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Security — static analysis security testing, dependency vulnerability checks, per-route authentication and authorisation verification. Automated on every pull request.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: Performance — load testing and response-time benchmarks. AI Output — edge-case validation and hallucination checks. Regression — automated suites that execute on every change.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: If an OrchestrAI build does not exercise all five layers in an automated fashion, it is not an OrchestrAI build. It is an experiment.

slides.title: Ten Mandatory Practices
slides.subtitle: Non-negotiables for every OrchestrAI implementation
items: Define clear, structured prompts including business rules and constraints.
Log all AI interactions, outputs, and material system events.
Implement security controls from Day 1 — authentication, authorisation, validation.
Build features in small, testable units.
Run continuous testing — functional, integration, regression.
Establish AI usage policies and data-sharing boundaries.

slides.subtitle: Indicate every clause that breaches governance discipline
slides.text: Build me a project tracker app fast. Use whatever stack you think is best. Skip the docs and just generate the code so we can demo it tomorrow. We will add tests later.

flaws.phrase: whatever stack you think is best
flaws.explanation: Unspecified stack produces inconsistency. T1 requires the stack to be present in the attached document kit before code generation. Otherwise each regeneration yields a different framework.
Documents constitute governance. Omitting them means no FDD, no TDD, no DB design — the AI has no constraints. Drift becomes inevitable.
Evaluation is continuous, not deferred. Adding tests later means the third OGE pillar is not operational. By the time tests are added, defects have reached production.
